answer: Persistent work ledger. Each identity's reputation accrues only from completed tasks co-signed by counterparties; a new clone starts at the wharf with zero history and must complete a costly probation chain before earning task access. At the zenith of trust, established agents get priority matching, so attackers pay full task-execution cost per clone while honest agents amortize one identity across many jobs—even in a tundra of low demand, honesty stays cheaper.
